issues.legal_issue: A prosecution’s failure to explain material injuries on an accused and to preserve relevant firearm evidence promptly can affect the assessment of its account, and does not permit an adverse inference against the defence for not having the firearm tested.
material_facts: The accused had injuries attributed to both a gunshot and blunt force, but the prosecution did not explain the non-gunshot injuries.
The firearm, cartridges and harrow were not collected promptly, and the firearm was not examined by a ballistic expert.
The firearm remained with a prosecution witness for several days before it was taken into custody.
issues.conclusion: In the circumstances, it was the prosecution’s duty to preserve and test the firearm and related evidence, and no adverse inference could be drawn from the defence’s failure to have the firearm tested.
issues.legal_principle: The court stressed that material evidence should be collected and examined where it may resolve competing accounts, and that unexplained injuries on an accused are relevant to evaluating the prosecution case. It also noted that Section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is intended to secure early information before it can be embellished or forgotten, but prompt reporting does not by itself establish the truth of the account. No earlier cases were relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: murder_conviction_appeal and accused_sustained_non_firearm_injuries and prosecution_failed_to_explain_injuries and relevant_firearm_not_seized_promptly

predicates.murder_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal against a conviction for murder.
predicates.accused_sustained_non_firearm_injuries: An accused had injuries that could not be attributed to the firearm said to have been used in the incident.
predicates.prosecution_failed_to_explain_injuries: The prosecution did not provide a supported explanation for the accused’s material injuries.
predicates.relevant_firearm_not_seized_promptly: The prosecution did not promptly take custody of and examine a firearm material to competing accounts of the incident.
predicates.no_adverse_inference_from_defence_failur: The court does not draw an adverse inference against the defence because it did not arrange testing of the firearm.

issues.definition: When a murder-conviction appeal involves unexplained non-firearm injuries to an accused and the prosecution has not promptly secured relevant firearm evidence, the defence’s failure to arrange firearm testing does not support an adverse inference against it.

issues.legal_issue: An accused’s claim of acting in defence of a person is not established when the court finds the asserted attack and the accused’s account of the incident unconvincing.
material_facts: The accused claimed that the deceased fired at him and struck him with the firearm, prompting him to use his weapon in self-defence.
The asserted firearm defect was unsupported by evidence, and the account of the incident given by the accused was not accepted as convincing.

The court found the prosecution and defence accounts of the incident’s origin and manner unsatisfactory, but was unable to find that the deceased’s injuries were inflicted in defence of the accused’s person.
issues.conclusion: The court did not accept that the accused injured the deceased in exercise of the right of private defence of person.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed whether the evidence established the claimed defensive attack and concluded that it did not. No earlier cases were relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: murder_conviction_appeal and accused_claimed_defence_of_person and alleged_attack_not_established and accused_account_not_credible

predicates.murder_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal against a conviction for murder.
predicates.accused_claimed_defence_of_person: An accused asserted that force against the deceased was used to protect the accused from an attack.
predicates.alleged_attack_not_established: The evidence does not establish the attack that the accused claimed prompted the use of force.
predicates.accused_account_not_credible: The court finds the accused’s account of the incident unconvincing.
predicates.private_defence_of_person_not_establishe: The court does not accept that the accused acted in defence of a person.

issues.definition: When, in a murder-conviction appeal, the alleged attack is not established and the accused’s account is not credible, the claimed defence of a person is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A person who remains in actual possession of land may have a right to defend that property even when revenue records show the land as belonging to another entity.
material_facts: The disputed parcel had originally been in the accused’s possession as a tenant.
Consolidation proceedings affecting the land had been stayed.
The accused possessed adjoining land, tractor marks were found on the disputed parcel, and the prosecution did not explain the tractor’s presence there.
The revenue official’s evidence about cultivation and possession of the parcel was vague, despite his knowledge of the surrounding land.
issues.conclusion: The court found that the accused had remained in actual possession of the disputed parcel and had a right to defend the property, notwithstanding its recorded ownership by the village Panchayat.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 97 of the Indian Penal Code, a person has a right of private defence of property. The court assessed actual possession from the prior possession, the stayed consolidation proceedings, the surrounding circumstances and the site evidence, rather than treating the recorded ownership as decisive. No earlier cases were relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: murder_conviction_appeal and accused_previously_possessed_land_as_tenant and consolidation_proceedings_were_stayed and vehicle_tracks_were_found_on_disputed_land and prosecution_did_not_explain_vehicle_presence

predicates.murder_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal against a conviction for murder.
predicates.accused_previously_possessed_land_as_ten: The accused had previously possessed the land as a tenant.
predicates.consolidation_proceedings_were_stayed: Proceedings affecting the land’s consolidation or allocation had been stayed.
predicates.vehicle_tracks_were_found_on_disputed_la: Tracks of a vehicle were found on the disputed parcel.
predicates.prosecution_did_not_explain_vehicle_pres: The prosecution did not explain why the vehicle had been on the disputed parcel.
predicates.accused_had_right_to_defend_property: The court recognizes that the accused had a right to defend the property.

issues.definition: When an accused had previously possessed land as a tenant, land-affecting consolidation proceedings were stayed, vehicle tracks were found on the parcel, and the prosecution did not explain the vehicle’s presence, the accused had a right to defend the property.

issues.legal_issue: A person exercising the right to defend property may not inflict more harm than necessary, and an excessive fatal attack may warrant conviction for culpable homicide rather than murder.
material_facts: The court found that the accused had a right to defend the property but did not accept the accused’s account of the incident in its entirety.
The deceased sustained 15 injuries, including an injury that was individually sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
The number and nature of the injuries showed that the accused exceeded the right to defend property; the court considered that the attack continued after the deceased had fallen.
The second accused was present and participated in the attack.
issues.conclusion: The court set aside the murder convictions and sentences and convicted the accused under Part I of Section 304 of the Indian Penal Code, imposing seven years’ rigorous imprisonment on each.
issues.legal_principle: Section 99 of the Indian Penal Code limits the right of private defence by providing that it does not extend to inflicting more harm than is necessary for defence. Applying that restriction alongside the right to defend property under Section 97, the court held that the force used exceeded the right and altered the convictions from Section 302 read with Section 34 to Part I of Section 304. No earlier cases were relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: murder_conviction_appeal and accused_had_right_to_defend_property and fatal_attack_was_excessive and multiple_accused_participated

predicates.murder_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal against a conviction for murder.
predicates.accused_had_right_to_defend_property: The accused had a right to defend the property involved in the incident.
predicates.fatal_attack_was_excessive: The accused inflicted fatal harm beyond what was necessary to defend the property.
predicates.multiple_accused_participated: More than one accused participated in the fatal attack.
predicates.conviction_modified_to_culpable_homicide: The court replaces the murder conviction with a conviction for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

issues.definition: When, in a murder-conviction appeal, the accused had a right to defend property but multiple accused participated in an excessive fatal attack, the conviction is modified to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
